instruction.text: Draw a line between the sites of the Battle of Stamford Bridge and the Battle of Hastings.

feedback.end: Shortly after King Harold defeated Harald Hardrada at the Battle of Stamford Bridge, William, Duke of Normandy, invaded from the south.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: William decided to invade the South of England. This part of the Bayeux Tapestry shows his troops making preparations to invade.

hint.label: Bayeux Tapestry
hint.text: The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered piece of cloth almost 70 metres long that shows the events leading up to the Norman conquest of England in 1066.

atoms.text: William’s invasion came as a surprise to Harold, who had to move his weak and tired army quickly back down south to face William. On October 14th 1066, both sides met at the Battle of Hastings.
Both sides engaged in a fierce battle. William’s army was made up of more experienced and stronger soldiers that included archers, infantry and cavalry.

hint.label: Cavalry
hint.text: The cavalry were soldiers who fought on horseback.

atoms.text: King Harold’s army was too tired to hold off the Normans, and eventually they were defeated. King Harold was killed, and William became King of England. He was later given the nickname William the Conqueror.

hint.label: Did you know?
hint.text: A famous legend says that King Harold was killed after he was shot in the eye with an arrow! No one really knows the truth though.

atoms.a: What was the battle between William and Harold called?
What was the state of Harold’s army when they arrived at the battle?
Who won the Battle of Hastings and became King of England?
